title: Implement tenant-aware queue fallback and adaptive safeguards after GPU exhaustion
creator: Asha Patel
description: After the 2025-01-10 GPU exhaust incident that caused sustained request queueing and broad customer slowdowns, we need a set of deterministic fallback behaviors and adaptive safeguards that reduce blast radius when a hosted GPU pool approaches saturation. This ticket tracks design, telemetry, and implementation of tenant-aware queue fallback, fast-path evictions, and autoscaler hysteresis adjustments so that tenant fairness and latency SLOs degrade predictably rather than collapse.
impact: Hosted GPU pool hit 98% utilization, request queue depth increased from ~10 to ~8,200 across affected shards, 99th percentile generation latency rose from 120ms to 1.9s, throughput dropped ~42% during the event. Multiple enterprise customers saw error spikes and sustained tail-latency regressions.
root_cause: Combined effect of (1) a sudden tenant burst pattern with heavy prefetches and long sequence generation requests which amplified queue occupancy, (2) autoscaler hysteresis and scale-step limits delaying capacity during ramp, and (3) admission controller allowing prefetch and chaining requests to queue without tenant-aware caps leading to KV cache pollution and per-GPU slot starvation.
investigation_notes: Telemetry: correlating tenant_id=acme-inc bursts with spike start 2025-01-10T02:12Z; their average sequence length 1.9x normal; prefetch requests accounted for ~27% of queued tokens.
Autoscaler: minimum scale step set to +2 nodes and cooldown 5m; observed scale latency ~4m due to instance provisioning and container cold-starts.
Admission: current admission scores don't penalize prefetch-heavy requests; tenant slot caps are global but not enforced per active queue shard.
KV cache: cache eviction churn increased by 63% during event, causing repeated cold-cache token decoding work and higher GPU compute per request.
Repro: Synthetic replay (see dashboard link) reproduces queue resonance with 20% of traffic using long-seq prefetch behavior.
Customer comms: SRE sent status updates during incident; no SLA credit requests logged yet but several customers flagged impact to business-critical flows.
decisions: Adopt a two-tier fallback: (A) soft per-tenant queue caps with jittered backpressure for active tenants, (B) hard fallback that routes excess traffic to a cheaper/compatible model variant (cpu-quantized or smaller GPU class) when pool occupancy > 95%.
Introduce an admission multiplier that penalizes prefetch and chained requests to reduce queue amplification.
Tune autoscaler to allow opportunistic fast-priming (prewarm smaller burst nodes) and reduce cooldown for emergency scaling windows.
Require runbook update and a new incident play for 'GPU pool resonance' that includes tenant throttling and immediate model fallback steps.
